question: According to the Wyoming CDL Manual, when you don't have enough room to stop in an emergency, what should you generally do?
choice_a: Steer away from what's ahead — you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop
choice_b: Slam the brakes and hold them down no matter what
choice_c: Downshift and coast until the vehicle slows on its own
choice_d: Sound the horn and continue straight ahead
explanation: The manual states stopping is not always the safest thing to do in an emergency, and that a driver can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than they can stop.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.1 Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: To be ready to make a quick, safe emergency turn, the manual says a driver should:
choice_a: Keep one hand on the mirror adjustment at all times
choice_b: Keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times
choice_c: Keep a foot resting lightly on the brake pedal at all times
choice_d: Loosen the grip on the wheel to react faster
explanation: The manual says the best way to have both hands on the wheel in an emergency is to keep them there all the time, since a firm two-handed grip is needed to turn quickly.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.1 Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: Why does the manual warn against applying the brake while making a quick turn to avoid an obstacle?
choice_a: It drains the air brake reservoir
choice_b: It shortens tire tread life
choice_c: It's very easy to lock your wheels while turning, which can cause you to skid out of control
choice_d: It triggers a mandatory roadside inspection
explanation: The manual specifically warns not to apply the brake while turning because it's easy to lock the wheels while turning, and if that happens, the vehicle may skid out of control.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.1 Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: When forced to return to the road after driving on the shoulder, what does the manual say a driver should avoid doing?
choice_a: Signaling before merging back
choice_b: Checking the mirrors before returning
choice_c: Holding the wheel tightly
choice_d: Edging back onto the road gradually — the tires might grab unexpectedly and cause a loss of control
explanation: The manual instructs drivers not to edge gradually back onto the road because the tires might grab unexpectedly, causing loss of control; instead, turn sharply enough to get back on safely.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.1 Driving Emergencies, Leaving the Road

question: With the "controlled braking" method of stopping quickly, how should you apply the brakes?
choice_a: As hard as you can without locking the wheels, keeping steering wheel movements small
choice_b: In short, hard stabs regardless of whether the wheels lock
choice_c: Only with the parking brake
choice_d: Gradually, over several seconds, no matter the distance available
explanation: Controlled braking means applying the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels while keeping steering movements very small; if the wheels lock, release and reapply.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.2 How to Stop Quickly and Safely

question: With the "stab braking" method, what should you do once the wheels lock up?
choice_a: Continue holding the brake pedal down harder
choice_b: Release the brakes, then reapply them fully once the wheels start rolling again
choice_c: Pump the accelerator to regain traction
choice_d: Shift into neutral immediately
explanation: Stab braking means applying the brakes fully, releasing when the wheels lock, and reapplying fully as soon as the wheels start rolling again.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.2 How to Stop Quickly and Safely

question: According to the manual, how long can it take for the wheels to start rolling again after releasing the brakes during stab braking?
choice_a: About five seconds
choice_b: About three seconds
choice_c: Up to one second
choice_d: Up to one minute
explanation: The manual notes it can take up to one second for the wheels to start rolling after releasing the brakes; reapplying too soon prevents the vehicle from straightening out.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.2 How to Stop Quickly and Safely

question: The manual explains that "jamming on the brakes" in an emergency stop is dangerous because:
choice_a: It uses excessive brake fluid
choice_b: It is illegal under Wyoming traffic law
choice_c: It overheats the tires within seconds
choice_d: It keeps the wheels locked up and causes a skid, during which the vehicle cannot be controlled
explanation: The manual states emergency braking does not mean pushing the pedal as hard as possible, since that keeps the wheels locked, causes a skid, and a skidding vehicle cannot be controlled.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.2 How to Stop Quickly and Safely

question: Per the manual, most hydraulic brake failures occur for one of two reasons. What are they?
choice_a: Loss of hydraulic pressure or brake fade on long hills
choice_b: Flat tires or running low on fuel
choice_c: Engine overheating or a dead battery
choice_d: Worn wiper blades or a broken mirror
explanation: The manual states most hydraulic brake failures occur from loss of hydraulic pressure or from brake fade on long hills.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.3 Brake Failure

question: If a vehicle's brake pedal feels spongy or goes to the floor because of loss of hydraulic pressure, what does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Turn off the headlights to save power
choice_b: Downshift into a lower gear to help slow the vehicle
choice_c: Accelerate to bypass the malfunction
choice_d: Shift into park while the vehicle is still moving
explanation: The manual lists downshifting into a lower gear as one of the things a driver can do to help slow the vehicle when hydraulic pressure is lost.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.3 Brake Failure

question: When using the parking/emergency brake to slow a vehicle after hydraulic brake failure, what must the driver do at the same time?
choice_a: Turn off the engine completely
choice_b: Unbuckle the seatbelt
choice_c: Press the release button or pull the release lever so the brake pressure can be adjusted and the wheels kept from locking up
choice_d: Turn on the emergency flashers
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to press the release button or pull the release lever at the same time they use the parking brake so they can adjust pressure and prevent wheel lockup.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.3 Brake Failure

question: If a driver's brakes fail while going downhill and an escape ramp is available, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Avoid it, because escape ramps damage tires
choice_b: Only use it if traveling below 5 mph
choice_c: Wait to see if the vehicle slows down naturally first
choice_d: Use it — escape ramps typically use soft gravel or an uphill grade to bring the vehicle to a stop
explanation: The manual says a driver who loses brakes going downhill should use an escape ramp if available, noting ramps use soft gravel that resists motion or turn uphill to stop the vehicle.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.3 Brake Failure

question: If no escape ramp is available after brake failure on a downgrade, what does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Take the least hazardous escape route available, such as an open field or a side road that flattens out or turns uphill
choice_b: Steer toward oncoming traffic to signal for help
choice_c: Continue at the same speed until reaching a phone
choice_d: Turn off the engine and coast to a stop on the roadway
explanation: The manual states that if no escape ramp is available, the driver should take the least hazardous escape route, such as an open field or side road that flattens out or turns uphill, as soon as possible.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.3 Brake Failure

question: What sound does the manual describe as an easily recognized sign of tire failure?
choice_a: A whining sound from the transmission
choice_b: The loud "bang" of a blowout
choice_c: A rattling sound from the exhaust
choice_d: A squeal from the brake pads
explanation: The manual lists the loud "bang" of a blowout as an easily recognized sign of tire failure, advising drivers to assume it is their own vehicle whenever they hear one.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.4 Tire Failure

question: If the steering feels "heavy" while driving, the manual says this is probably a sign that:
choice_a: The power steering fluid is low
choice_b: The rear axle is overloaded
choice_c: One of the front tires has failed
choice_d: The ABS system has just activated
explanation: The manual states that if the steering feels heavy, it is probably a sign that one of the front tires has failed.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.4 Tire Failure

question: Immediately after a tire fails, what does the manual say about using the brakes?
choice_a: Brake as hard as possible right away
choice_b: Pump the brakes rapidly and continuously
choice_c: Use only the parking brake
choice_d: Stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed down, then brake very gently, pull off the road, and stop
explanation: The manual warns that braking when a tire has failed could cause loss of control, so the driver should stay off the brake until slowed, then brake gently and pull off the road.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.4 Tire Failure

question: After stopping following a suspected tire failure, what does the manual say a driver should do, even if the vehicle seems to be handling fine?
choice_a: Get out and check all the tires, since a dual tire failure may only be noticeable by looking
choice_b: Continue driving until reaching the next town
choice_c: Only check the tire that made the loudest noise
choice_d: Call for a replacement tire without inspecting anything
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to get out and check all the tires after stopping, because if one of a set of dual tires has failed, looking at it may be the only way to know.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.17.4 Tire Failure

question: What is the primary function of an Anti-lock Braking System (ABS), per the manual?
choice_a: It increases a vehicle's normal braking power beyond standard brakes
choice_b: It keeps the wheels from locking up during hard brake applications
choice_c: It automatically steers the vehicle around obstacles
choice_d: It replaces the need for regular brakes entirely
explanation: The manual defines ABS as a computerized system that keeps the wheels from locking up during hard brake applications; it does not decrease or increase normal braking capability.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.18 Anti-lock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Does ABS necessarily shorten a vehicle's stopping distance, according to the manual?
choice_a: Yes, it always cuts stopping distance in half
choice_b: Yes, but only above 50 mph
choice_c: No — ABS does not necessarily shorten stopping distance, but it does help keep the vehicle under control during hard braking
choice_d: No, ABS has no effect on braking whatsoever
explanation: The manual explicitly states ABS does not necessarily shorten stopping distance, but it does help drivers keep the vehicle under control during hard braking.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.18 Anti-lock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Per the manual, ABS is required on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after what date?
choice_a: January 1, 1990
choice_b: March 1, 2000
choice_c: June 1, 1995
choice_d: March 1, 1997
explanation: The manual states the Department of Transportation requires ABS on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.18.2 Vehicles Required to Have Anti-lock Braking Systems

question: On trailers, where is the yellow ABS malfunction lamp located, per the manual?
choice_a: On the left side, either the front or rear corner
choice_b: On the dashboard inside the cab
choice_c: Centered on the rear bumper
choice_d: Inside the trailer's cargo compartment
explanation: The manual states trailers will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.18.3 How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS

question: If the ABS malfunction lamp stays on after the bulb check, or comes on while driving, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: The vehicle must be towed immediately and cannot be driven
choice_b: You may have lost ABS control on one or more wheels; drive normally on your regular brakes and get the system serviced soon
choice_c: The parking brake will engage automatically to stop the vehicle
choice_d: The trailer must be disconnected before continuing
explanation: The manual explains that if the lamp stays on or comes on while driving, ABS control may be lost, but regular brakes still work — drive normally and have the system serviced soon.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.18.3 How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS

question: According to the manual, what is the one exception that allows a driver to fully apply the brakes in an emergency stop?
choice_a: Driving on wet pavement
choice_b: Driving a bus that is below passenger capacity
choice_c: Driving a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles
choice_d: Driving under 20 mph
explanation: The manual states there is only one exception to the normal ABS braking procedure: if you drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, you can fully apply the brakes in an emergency stop.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.18.6 Braking with ABS

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as one of the four causes of skids?
choice_a: Using headlights at night
choice_b: Maintaining proper following distance
choice_c: Correct tire inflation
choice_d: Over-braking — braking too hard and locking up the wheels
explanation: The manual lists over-braking, defined as braking too hard and locking up the wheels, as one of the four causes of skids.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.19 Skid Control and Recovery

question: Per the manual, what is the source of most serious skids?
choice_a: Driving too fast for road conditions
choice_b: Worn windshield wipers
choice_c: Using cruise control on the highway
choice_d: Low windshield washer fluid
explanation: The manual states that most serious skids result from driving too fast for road conditions, since drivers who adjust to conditions avoid needing to over-brake, over-steer, or over-accelerate.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.19 Skid Control and Recovery

question: What does the manual describe as "by far the most common skid"?
choice_a: A skid where only the steering wheel loses grip
choice_b: One in which the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration
choice_c: A skid caused solely by worn wiper blades
choice_d: A skid from an overinflated spare tire
explanation: The manual identifies the drive-wheel skid, where the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration, as by far the most common skid.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.19.1 Drive-Wheel Skids

question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, the manual says the first step is to:
choice_a: Turn the steering wheel as sharply as possible
choice_b: Apply the parking brake fully
choice_c: Stop braking, which lets the rear wheels roll again and keeps them from sliding
choice_d: Accelerate hard to regain traction
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop braking first when correcting a drive-wheel braking skid, since this lets the rear wheels roll again and keeps them from sliding sideways.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.19.2 Correcting a Drive-Wheel Braking Skid

question: The manual states that the only way to stop a front-wheel skid is to:
choice_a: Turn the steering wheel harder in the direction of the skid
choice_b: Apply the brakes firmly
choice_c: Shift into a higher gear
choice_d: Let the vehicle slow down — stop turning and/or braking so hard
explanation: The manual explains that in a front-wheel skid the only way to stop it is to let the vehicle slow down, which means easing off both steering and braking effort.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.19.3 Front-Wheel Skids

question: What is the first thing to do at a crash scene, per the manual's basic crash procedures?
choice_a: Keep another crash from happening in the same spot
choice_b: Take photographs for the insurance report
choice_c: Exchange contact information with the other driver
choice_d: Call your dispatcher for instructions
explanation: The manual states the first thing to do at a crash scene is to protect the area — keep another crash from happening in the same spot.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.20.1 Protect the Area

question: If a driver has a cell phone or CB radio when involved in a crash, when should they call for assistance?
choice_a: Only after all vehicles have been moved off the road
choice_b: Before getting out of the vehicle
choice_c: Only if there are visible injuries
choice_d: Wait for another driver to call first
explanation: The manual instructs drivers with a cell phone or CB to call for assistance before getting out of the vehicle.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.20.2 Notify Authorities

question: According to the manual, when should you avoid moving a severely injured person at a crash scene?
choice_a: Never move them under any circumstances
choice_b: Move them right away regardless of conditions
choice_c: Unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary
choice_d: Only a doctor is permitted to move them
explanation: The manual says not to move a severely injured person unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.20.3 Care for the Injured

question: How does the manual say to stop heavy bleeding when caring for an injured person?
choice_a: Elevate the affected limb only
choice_b: Apply a tourniquet in every case
choice_c: Wrap the wound loosely with cloth
choice_d: Apply direct pressure to the wound
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop heavy bleeding by applying direct pressure to the wound.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.20.3 Care for the Injured

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as a cause of vehicle fires?
choice_a: Under-inflated tires and duals that touch
choice_b: A fully charged fire extinguisher
choice_c: A recently completed pre-trip inspection
choice_d: Properly sealed and loaded cargo
explanation: The manual lists under-inflated tires and duals that touch as one of the causes of vehicle fires.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.21.1 Causes of Fire

question: If an engine catches fire, what does the manual advise a driver to do?
choice_a: Open the hood right away to see the flames
choice_b: Turn off the engine as soon as possible, avoid opening the hood, and shoot foam through the louvers, radiator, or underside
choice_c: Pour water directly onto the engine block
choice_d: Keep driving until reaching a repair shop
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to turn off the engine as soon as they can, avoid opening the hood, and shoot foam through the louvers, radiator, or the vehicle's underside for an engine fire.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.21.3 Fire Fighting

question: For a cargo fire in a van or box trailer carrying hazardous materials, what does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Open the rear doors to vent the smoke
choice_b: Spray water directly into the trailer
choice_c: Keep the doors shut, since opening them supplies the fire with oxygen and can make it burn faster
choice_d: Continue driving at highway speed to blow out the fire
explanation: The manual says to keep the doors shut on a van or box trailer cargo fire, especially with hazardous materials, because opening the doors supplies oxygen and can cause the fire to burn very fast.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.21.3 Fire Fighting

question: When using a fire extinguisher, where should you aim it, per the manual?
choice_a: Up into the flames
choice_b: At the thickest part of the smoke
choice_c: Anywhere within a few feet of the fire
choice_d: At the source or base of the fire, not up in the flames
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to aim the extinguisher at the source or base of the fire, not up into the flames.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.21.3 Fire Fighting

question: According to Figure 2.20 in the manual, a Class D fire (fires in combustible metals) should be extinguished by:
choice_a: Using specialized extinguishing powders
choice_b: Spraying with plain water
choice_c: Smothering with a wool blanket only
choice_d: Using a garden hose
explanation: Figure 2.20 in the manual states Class D fires (combustible metals) are extinguished by using specialized extinguishing powders.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.21.3 Fire Fighting, Figure 2.20 Class/Type of Fires

question: Per the manual, how much alcohol can the human liver process per hour?
choice_a: A full standard drink
choice_b: One-third an ounce of alcohol
choice_c: Two full drinks
choice_d: It depends only on body temperature
explanation: The manual states the liver can only process one-third an ounce of alcohol per hour, which is considerably less than the alcohol in a standard drink.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.22.1 Alcohol and Driving, How Alcohol Works

question: What does the manual say actually sobers a person up after drinking, since the liver processes alcohol at a fixed rate?
choice_a: Black coffee
choice_b: A cold shower
choice_c: Only time
choice_d: Vigorous exercise
explanation: The manual states that because the liver processes alcohol at a fixed rate, only time — not black coffee or a cold shower — will sober a person up.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.22.1 Alcohol and Driving, How Alcohol Works

question: The manual states that crashes involving people who have been drinking alcohol result in how many deaths every year?
choice_a: About 2,000
choice_b: About 200
choice_c: About 5,000
choice_d: Over 20,000
explanation: The manual states people who drink alcohol are involved in traffic crashes resulting in over 20,000 deaths every year.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.22.1 Alcohol and Driving

question: According to Figure 2.23 in the manual, which BAC level is identified as the "drunk driving limit," with definite impairment in coordination and judgment?
explanation: Figure 2.23 shows that at .08 BAC, there is definite impairment in coordination and judgment, labeled as the drunk driving limit.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.22.1 Alcohol and Driving, Figure 2.23 Effects of Increasing Blood Alcohol Content

question: Per the manual's list of drinks containing the same amount of alcohol, which of the following is included?
choice_a: A 16-ounce glass of soda
choice_b: A 12-ounce glass of beer with 5 percent alcohol content
choice_c: A 2-ounce shot of 40-proof liquor
choice_d: A 20-ounce energy drink
explanation: The manual lists a 12-ounce glass of beer with a 5 percent alcohol content as one of three drinks (along with wine and liquor) that contain the same amount of alcohol.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.22.1 Alcohol and Driving

question: According to the manual, when is a driver permitted to use a drug given to them by a doctor?
choice_a: Never, regardless of the circumstances
choice_b: Only if it is an over-the-counter drug
choice_c: If the doctor informs the driver that it will not affect safe driving ability
choice_d: Only on days the driver is not scheduled to drive
explanation: The manual states that possession and use of a drug given to a driver by a doctor is permitted if the doctor informs the driver it will not affect safe driving ability.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.22.2 Other Drugs

question: The manual warns that some legal drugs, such as cold medicines, can have what effect that is a driving concern?
choice_a: They improve reaction time
choice_b: They increase night vision
choice_c: They cause euphoria only
choice_d: They may make the driver drowsy or otherwise affect safe driving ability
explanation: The manual notes that prescription and over-the-counter drugs, including cold medicines, may make a driver drowsy or otherwise affect safe driving ability.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.22.2 Other Drugs

question: Per the manual, what is the "safest rule" regarding drugs and driving?
choice_a: Don't mix drugs with driving at all
choice_b: Only use drugs that don't cause drowsiness
choice_c: Take drugs only in small doses before driving
choice_d: Combine caffeine with any needed medication
explanation: The manual states the safest rule is don't mix drugs with driving at all, noting alcohol can make the effects of other drugs much worse.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.22.2 Other Drugs

question: If a driver becomes too ill to operate a motor vehicle safely, what does the manual say they must do?
choice_a: Continue driving carefully at a reduced speed
choice_b: Not drive
choice_c: Ask a passenger to steer while they rest
choice_d: Drive only on local roads
explanation: The manual states that if a driver becomes so ill they cannot operate a vehicle safely, they must not drive.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.22.3 Illness

question: What exception does the manual allow for a driver who becomes too ill to drive safely?
choice_a: They may continue their full route at reduced speed
choice_b: They may drive if a passenger stays awake to watch the road
choice_c: In case of an emergency, they may drive to the nearest place where they can safely stop
choice_d: They may drive as long as they use cruise control
explanation: The manual's only exception allows a driver who is too ill to drive to, in an emergency, drive to the nearest place where they can safely stop.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.22.3 Illness

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Drivers
question: What must every commercial driver be able to do regarding hazardous cargo, per the manual's hazardous materials rules for all commercial drivers?
choice_a: Ignore hazardous cargo rules unless hazmat-endorsed
choice_b: Assume the shipper has already verified safety
choice_c: Rely solely on dispatch to identify hazardous cargo
choice_d: Recognize hazardous cargo and know whether they can haul it without a hazardous materials endorsement
explanation: The manual states all drivers should know something about hazardous materials, and must be able to recognize hazardous cargo and know whether they can haul it without a hazardous materials endorsement.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.23 Hazardous Materials Rules For All Commercial Drivers

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Drivers
question: Per the manual, hazardous materials shipping papers must be kept:
choice_a: Tabbed and in a pouch on the driver's door, in clear view within reach, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle
choice_b: Locked in the glovebox at all times
choice_c: Mailed ahead to the delivery site
choice_d: In the sleeper berth only
explanation: The manual requires tabbing hazardous materials shipping papers and keeping them in a pouch on the driver's door, in clear view within reach while driving, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.23.2 Why Are There Rules?

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Drivers
question: What is the minimum number of identical placards a placarded vehicle must display, and where?
choice_a: Two placards, front and rear only
choice_b: At least four identical placards — on the front, rear, and both sides
choice_c: One placard, on the driver's door
choice_d: Six placards, two on each side
explanation: The manual states a placarded vehicle must have at least four identical placards, placed on the front, rear, and both sides, readable from all four directions.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.23.3 Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Drivers
question: Per the manual, placards must be at least what size and shape?
choice_a: 6 inches square, circular
choice_b: 8 inches square, triangular
choice_c: 10 3/4 inches square, turned upright on a point in a diamond shape
choice_d: 12 inches square, rectangular
explanation: The manual states placards must be at least 10 3/4 inches square, turned upright on a point, in a diamond shape.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.23.3 Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Drivers
question: An identification number used by first responders to identify hazardous materials is a four-digit code preceded by which letters, per the manual?
choice_a: "HZ" or "MC"
choice_b: "DOT" or "CDL"
choice_c: "FM" or "EX"
choice_d: "NA" or "UN"
explanation: The manual states identification numbers are four-digit codes preceded by the letters "NA" or "UN," used by first responders and identified in the ERG.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.23.3 Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Drivers
question: According to Figure 2.24 in the manual, which hazard class includes examples like gasoline fuel and acetone?
choice_a: Class 3 — Flammable
choice_b: Class 6 — Poisons
choice_c: Class 8 — Corrosives
choice_d: Class 1 — Explosives
explanation: Figure 2.24's hazard class definitions list Class 3 Flammable with examples of gasoline fuel and acetone.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.23.3 Lists of Regulated Products, Figure 2.24 Hazard Class Definitions

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Drivers
question: Per the manual, can a driver operate a vehicle carrying hazardous materials that does not require placards without a hazardous materials endorsement?
choice_a: No, an endorsement is always required for any amount of hazardous material
choice_b: Yes — you can drive it if it does not require placards; if it does require placards, you need the hazardous materials endorsement
choice_c: Only with written permission from WYDOT for each trip
choice_d: Only if the load weighs under 100 pounds
explanation: The manual explains that not all hazmat-carrying vehicles require placards, and a driver can operate one that doesn't; but if placards are required, the driver must have the hazardous materials endorsement.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.23.3 Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Drivers
question: Per the manual, a tank endorsement is required for a vehicle needing a Class A or B CDL with a permanently mounted cargo tank, or one carrying a portable tank with a capacity of at least how many gallons?
choice_a: 500 gallons
choice_b: 750 gallons
choice_c: 1,000 gallons
choice_d: 2,000 gallons
explanation: The manual states a tank endorsement is required if the vehicle needs a Class A or B CDL and has a permanently mounted cargo tank of any capacity, or carries a portable tank with a capacity of 1,000 gallons or more.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 2 — subsection 2.23.3 Lists of Regulated Products
